title: Differential attention kernel probabilistic selector for MIG fragmentation
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem statement: On mixed-SKU fleets (H100/L40S/A10) with aggressive MIG partitioning we observe increased tail latency and kernel churn for prefill-heavy workloads. Existing deterministic kernel selection favors single highest-throughput kernel which causes repeated kernel swaps across MIG slice boundaries and frequent clock domain shifts, increasing prefill p99 and decode tail. We need a low-risk selector that reduces churn by incorporating MIG fragmentation, SKU-specific warmup costs, attention sparsity, and sequence-length distribution into kernel choice.
technical_design: High-level approach: implement a probabilistic kernel selector that ranks candidate kernels by an expected-cost score and samples among the top-N candidates with a temperature that depends on MIG fragmentation and observed warmup penalty. Inputs: kernel throughput profile per SKU, measured kernel warmup cost (ms) per MIG slice, per-request features (seq_len, prefix_hit_rate, attention_sparsity_estimate from tokenizer heuristics), current clock state tag. Score composition: expected_token_cost = latency_per_token / quantile_throughput_adjustment + warmup_penalty * P(warmup_needed). Selector policy: when MIG fragmentation ratio > threshold OR warmup_penalty high, increase sampling temperature to prefer stability; otherwise greedily pick highest scored kernel. Eviction scheduler: when migrating among kernels, coalesce prefill batches to minimize cross-slice context loads and prefer kernel pairings that reuse KV layouts. Implementation notes: 1) lightweight prober agent runs at slice boot to estimate warmup_ms per kernel per MIG slice and reports to local shard cache; 2) selector implemented as a runtime policy plugin with a small C++ hot path and a configurable Java/Python control-plane policy for tuning; 3) add metrics hooks for chosen_kernel, candidate_scores, sampling_temperature, and evictions_per_minute. Backward compatibility: default to current deterministic selector until rollout is progressive. Rollback by toggling selector gate to "deterministic".
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end experiment shows >=8% reduction in prefill p99 on mixed MIG fleets (H100 & L40S) for representative workloads
2) No more than 1% regression in median latency for throughput-oriented workloads on A10 SKU
3) Kernel churn (kernel swaps per 10k requests) reduced by >=30% in MIG-fragmented setups
4) Telemetry events for chosen_kernel and sampling_temperature show sane distributions (no pathological oscillation), and logs include warmup_ms estimates per slice
5) Selector can be toggled off via runtime feature gate without requiring model reloads
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + microbench harness for score computation (local CI)
Phase 1: Canary on internal testing fleet with synthetic prefill-heavy traces (5% traffic) for 48h
Phase 2: Regional pilot on customer-similar clusters (per-SKU pilot: H100-L40S mixed, then A10-only) under shadow mode for 72h
Phase 3: A/B experiment (10% traffic) measuring p50/p95/p99 and kernel churn, run for 7 days
Phase 4: Ramp to 50% then 100% if success criteria met; otherwise roll back to deterministic selector
risks: Warmup estimates may be noisy for low-traffic slices leading to suboptimal choices; mitigated by conservative priors and decay windows
Increased CPU overhead in hot path if selector evaluation is not optimized; mitigate by inlining scoring math and bounding candidate set to top-3
Edge cases: extreme attention sparsity heuristics might misclassify dense attention causing throughput loss; include safety checks to fall back to deterministic kernel for skewed signals
Cross-slice telemetry volume increase — limit sampling frequency for detailed candidate_scores to 1% of requests
notes: We reuse the existing kernel profile store but extend schema with per-mig-slice warmup_ms and last_probed_at timestamp
Consider exposing a console toggle for sampling_temperature and top-N to SRE for fast remediation
This selector complements (does not replace) the kernel fingerprint routing work; coordinate with that team to share probe data
